source: DHS Yearbook of Immigration Statistics, DOJ EOIR, CBP, DOS Visa Statistics

countries.name: Mexico
countries.overview: Mexico is by far the largest source of immigrants to the United States, with over 10.7 million Mexican-born residents. The deep economic and geographic ties between the two countries drive both legal and unauthorized migration. Mexican nationals face among the longest green card wait times due to per-country caps and massive demand.
keyFacts: Largest source country for U.S. immigration
21+ year wait for family-sponsored green cards
Accounts for ~23% of all foreign-born U.S. residents

countries.name: Guatemala
countries.overview: Guatemala has become one of the top source countries for asylum seekers and border encounters. Gang violence, poverty, and climate disasters drive migration. Guatemalan nationals are among the most represented in immigration court.
keyFacts: Second most cases in immigration court

countries.name: Honduras
countries.overview: Honduras, one of the Northern Triangle countries, has experienced massive outmigration driven by gang violence, corruption, and economic instability. The country was heavily impacted by Hurricanes Eta and Iota in 2020.
keyFacts: Third highest case volume in immigration courts
Northern Triangle country with high asylum volume

countries.name: El Salvador
countries.overview: El Salvador has a long history of migration to the U.S., driven initially by civil war in the 1980s and later by gang violence. The country has one of the largest TPS populations. Recent gang crackdowns under President Bukele have shifted dynamics.
keyFacts: Civil war drove initial migration wave
Gang violence historically major push factor
Bukele crackdown may reduce asylum claims

countries.name: Venezuela
countries.overview: Venezuela experienced the fastest growth in immigration court cases of any nationality. The collapse of the Maduro regime drove millions into exile. Venezuelans have higher asylum grant rates than Central American nationalities. Deportation is complicated by lack of diplomatic relations.
keyFacts: Difficult to deport due to diplomatic issues
Higher asylum grant rate than Central Americans

countries.name: Cuba
countries.overview: Cuban immigration has a unique legal history due to the Cuban Adjustment Act and wet-foot/dry-foot policy (ended 2017). Cuban asylum seekers historically received favorable treatment. The 2022-2023 migration surge brought record numbers.
keyFacts: Cuban Adjustment Act provides special pathway

countries.name: Colombia
countries.overview: Colombia has become a major source country for both legal and unauthorized migration. The end of the FARC conflict paradoxically increased migration as rural areas remained unstable. Colombia also serves as a transit country for Venezuelan migrants.

countries.name: India
countries.overview: India is the second-largest source of immigrants to the U.S. and the dominant source of H-1B skilled worker visas. Indian nationals face the longest green card backlogs of any country — over 50 years for employment-based categories due to per-country caps.
keyFacts: 50+ year green card backlog for EB categories
Growing asylum claims from religious minorities

countries.name: China
countries.overview: Chinese immigration to the U.S. spans skilled workers, students, investors, and asylum seekers. China is the largest source of international students. Asylum claims often cite political persecution, religious freedom, and the one-child policy.

countries.name: Philippines
countries.overview: The Philippines is a top source of family-sponsored immigration, reflecting deep historical ties from U.S. colonial rule. Filipino nurses are a major component of the U.S. healthcare workforce. Family visa backlogs extend over 20 years.

countries.name: Haiti
countries.overview: Haitian immigration has been shaped by repeated crises — earthquakes, political instability, and gang violence. Haiti has been designated for TPS multiple times. Despite severe conditions, Haitian asylum grant rates remain relatively low.
keyFacts: TPS designated due to ongoing crises
Low asylum grant rate despite severe conditions
2021 Del Rio bridge crisis drew attention

countries.name: Dominican Republic
countries.overview: Dominican immigration is heavily family-based, concentrated in the New York metro area. The community has deep roots dating back to the 1960s. Most Dominican immigration is legal, through family sponsorship.
keyFacts: Heavily concentrated in NYC metro area

countries.name: Brazil
countries.overview: Brazilian immigration has grown significantly, with increasing numbers entering through the southern border. Brazil is also one of the largest tourist visa recipients. The community is concentrated in Massachusetts, Florida, and New Jersey.
keyFacts: Growing border crossings from Brazilian nationals

countries.name: Nicaragua
countries.overview: Nicaraguan migration surged after the 2018 political crisis under President Ortega. The country has been designated for TPS. Many Nicaraguans claim asylum based on political persecution.
keyFacts: High rate of political asylum claims

countries.name: Ecuador
countries.overview: Ecuadorian migration has increased dramatically, driven by rising gang violence and economic instability. Ecuador declared a state of emergency in 2024. The community is concentrated in the New York metro area.
keyFacts: Sharp increase in border encounters since 2022

countries.name: Jamaica
countries.overview: Jamaican immigration is primarily family-based and has deep historical roots. The community is concentrated in New York, Florida, and Connecticut. Jamaica is also a significant source of H-2B seasonal workers.
keyFacts: Strong community in NYC and South Florida

countries.name: South Korea
countries.overview: Korean immigration has deep roots from the post-Korean War era. The community is concentrated in Los Angeles, New York, and the Washington D.C. metro. Korea is a major source of students and skilled workers.

countries.name: Vietnam
countries.overview: Vietnamese immigration stems largely from the refugee resettlement after the Vietnam War. Family reunification continues to drive migration. Vietnam has long visa backlogs in family-sponsored categories.
keyFacts: Refugee origins from Vietnam War era
Strong community in CA, TX, WA

countries.name: Peru
countries.overview: Peruvian migration has increased amid political instability following the ouster of President Castillo in 2022. The community is concentrated in the New York, New Jersey, and South Florida areas.
keyFacts: Concentrated in tri-state area and Florida

countries.name: Ukraine
countries.overview: Ukrainian immigration surged after Russia's 2022 invasion, with the U.S. creating the Uniting for Ukraine parole program. Ukrainians have among the highest asylum grant rates. The community has historical roots from earlier immigration waves.
keyFacts: Highest asylum grant rate among major nationalities
Historical community in Chicago, NYC, Sacramento
